properties.name: Many people on one project AND many projects at once — the two axes must hold TOGETHER, which neither accepted requirement says
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-05, stating what flo2 actually is: "a web app that has reflow2 as its core service... you will probably have multiple people working simultaneously on the same project - and secondly, you could have multiple different projects going on through the web app simultaneously. reflow2 needs to support both."

BOTH AXES ARE ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT, SEPARATELY. Axis one is req:sessions-share-a-graph — "several sessions on one machine work the same design at the same time" — accepted, and already realized: cap:shared-sessions is VERIFIED, serving many sessions from one process over --http, and it satisfies single-writer rather than working around it because one server means exactly one writer. Axis two is req:many-designs-one-service — "one reflow2 can hold several designs, and a session says which one it is working on" — accepted, and deliberately silent on where the designs live.

WHAT IS MISSING IS THE COMPOSITION, AND IT IS NOT IMPLIED BY EITHER. Nothing in the design states that N people across M projects works — only that N people on ONE project works, and that M projects can be held. The cross product is a distinct claim with distinct failure modes, and flo2 is the first consumer that needs it.

THE CONCRETE QUESTION THE COMPOSITION RAISES, which the flo2 proposal does not answer: LOCK GRANULARITY. req:sessions-share-a-graph requires that "reads must not queue behind each other (the graph sits behind a lock that today serialises everything)", and cap:shared-sessions met that by moving the graph from a Mutex to an RwLock — PER PROCESS, holding one graph. Once one process holds many graphs, a per-process lock would make a write on project A block reads on project B, which is a cross-tenant performance coupling that neither requirement forbids because neither one can see it. The registry map itself must not become the new serialisation point. The property that has to hold: concurrency is per-design, so activity on one project is invisible in the latency of another.

RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME AS ISOLATION. req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph is about CORRECTNESS and security — project A's design must be unreachable from project B's session. This requirement is about CONCURRENCY — project A's traffic must not degrade project B's. A design can have either without the other, and a hosted service needs both.

NOTE ON WHAT "MANY PEOPLE" NOW MEANS. req:sessions-share-a-graph was written for "several sessions ON ONE MACHINE" (Anthony, 2026-07-26, six concurrent sessions on his own box). flo2 makes them several people on several machines reaching one hosted process, which keeps the single-writer property intact — there is still exactly one writer, the server — but changes who the seats belong to and puts req:seat-per-client under real load rather than local load.
